statement: For iid Bernoulli bond percolation on the undirected infinite path G=(Z,{{n,n+1}:n in Z}), G is connected, locally finite and vertex-transitive, p_c(G)=1, and theta_G(p_c)=1. Thus theta_G(p_c)=0 for every infinite locally finite quasi-transitive graph is false unless additional assumptions exclude this case.
assumptions: theta_G(p)=P_p(0 belongs to an infinite open component)
proof: For p<1, an infinite component containing 0 requires all edges on at least one of the two infinite rays from 0 to be open. For either ray the probability is lim_{n->infinity}p^n=0, so theta_G(p)=0 by a union bound. At p=1 every edge is open almost surely, hence theta_G(1)=1 and p_c=1.
remaining_gap: Exact restricted target recovered; only the referee check is pending. This refutes the unqualified formulation, not the p_c<1 conjecture.

statement: For every fixed a in (0,1), the array f_n(p)=min{1,(p/a)^n}, p in [0,1], n>=1, is continuous and increasing in p and decreasing in n, satisfies inf_n f_n(a)=1, and satisfies inf_n f_n(q)=0 for every q<a. Consequently positivity at a and continuity of each finite-scale function do not imply a single q<a with positive infimum over all scales.
assumptions: abstract array of scalar functions; no claim that these are target-graph percolation probabilities
proof: At p=a every term equals 1. At q<a the ratio q/a is in [0,1), whose nth power tends to 0. Continuity, parameter monotonicity and scale monotonicity follow directly from the formula.
remaining_gap: Referee check; this only refutes the abstract quantifier interchange and is not a counterexample to P0043.

statement: Let G be an infinite connected graph of maximum degree Delta<infinity and limsup_r |B_G(o,r)|^(1/r)=1. For every infinite connected subgraph H of G containing o, the anchored edge-isoperimetric constant iota_*(H,o), defined using finite connected vertex sets containing o, equals zero.
assumptions: subexponential ambient volume growth at o
rooted finite connected sets in the definition of anchored expansion
proof: If iota_*>0, there exist c>0 and n0 such that every rooted finite connected S of size at least n0 has boundary_H(S)>=c|S|. Apply this to H-balls, whose sizes grow unboundedly. Since outside vertices have degree at most Delta, |B_H(o,r+1)| >= (1+c/Delta)|B_H(o,r)| eventually. This forces exponential H-ball growth, contradicting B_H(o,r) subset B_G(o,r) and subexponential G-ball growth.
remaining_gap: Referee check; this obstructs positive-anchored-expansion routes but does not establish P0043 on subexponential graphs.

statement: Let G=(V,E) be a finite graph, mu a probability law on {0,1}^E, and q in [0,1]. Fix an exploration e(omega) ordering every edge once, with deterministic first edge and each next edge determined only by previously revealed edge indices and bits. For each complete transcript (a,x) with positive mu probability, let Expl_k(a,x) denote agreement with its first k revealed edge indices and bits. Suppose mu(omega_{a_{k+1}}=1 | Expl_k(a,x))>=q for every such transcript and every k=0,...,|E|-1. Then iid Bernoulli-q on E is stochastically dominated by mu: for every increasing event A, P_q(A)<=mu(A).
assumptions: finite graph G and finite edge set E
later edge choices depend only on revealed indices and bits
conditional next-edge lower bound q at every prefix of every positive-probability complete transcript

source.type: primary-source-checked correction of a stored concept fragment
source.author: Hugo Vanneuville

proof: Induct on |E|. Condition on the deterministic first bit; each positive-probability branch inherits the same history-wise bound on the remaining adaptive exploration. Apply the inductive domination to the restrictions A^0 subset A^1 of an increasing event A. The first bit has probability at least q, so the mixture is at least (1-q)P_q(A^0)+qP_q(A^1)=P_q(A). Ignore zero-probability branches, whose mixture coefficient is zero. The empty edge set is immediate.
remaining_gap: Referee checks the corrected standalone statement. An infinite critical-cluster bridge additionally needs uniform bounds, a percolating comparison object and justified infinite limits.
